items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: And I think that was one of the reasons Howard left the band. Because I wasn’t that warm to his compositions.

ctx.x: If someone brings a tune of their own to the group, they’re emotionally invested in it, but it’s just not a Flecktone song, is it really apparent to everybody?

It’s not always apparent. And it’s the difficult thing about being a leader is that I might have that feeling but I have to be suspicious of myself too. Because I have to make sure that I haven’t, maybe I don’t think I sound good on it or something. But I have to sound good on it too. Or I might not think it’s that great a song or something and I have to like, sometimes I have an instinctive thing, it’s just, I just don’t like it. And what am I going to do? Am I going to say something and like be a downer? Or am…

You’ve probably played a number of times in well known music schools, universities and so forth. Do you wonder what some of the people that are majoring in jazz now and so forth are going to do when they get out? Knowing what you do about the music business?

items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: he was a founding member of Bela Fleck & the Flecktones

ctx.x: Howard Levy is a two time Grammy award winner, pianist, composer, and master of the diatonic harmonica. In addition to his own recordings as a leader, he was a founding member of Bela Fleck & the Flecktones, and has appeared on a lengthy list of recordings by other major artists.
Howard was interviewed via Zoom on November 11, 2025 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
